transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-01-05
- Start: 17:00 UTC
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood Solutions), Priya (Head of Search, NeoQuest), Omar (ML Eng), Lena (CTO), Diego (SRE)

Summary:
Priya and team run a product search stack (hybrid retrieval + rerank) and are evaluating where to host embeddings + rerank: Redwood Hosted for fast tryout, Dedicated for predictable throughput, or Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency. Primary constraints: tail latency SLO for reranking (~150-250ms), cost per request, and integration with existing vector DB (self-hosted Milvus today). They're looking for pilot pricing, security docs, and a benchmark with ~500k docs and 200 QPS-ish ingestion/serve pattern.

Topics covered (auto sections may be noisy):
- Current stack: milvus + elastic + custom reranker
- Embedding dim tradeoffs (1536 vs 768 vs 512)
- Fanout + hybrid search vs single-stage rerank economics
- Where to serve embeddings: close to vector DB vs centralize in Redwood
- Redis/KV cache vs Redwood prefix cache
- Security: SSO, SOC 2, KMS, audit logs

Action items recap (brief): Maya to send pricing + security pack; Daniel to script benchmark and run smoke; Priya to share dataset.

Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Maya: all right cool thanks everyone for making time, uh before we dive in quick round robin? I think we have Priya, Omar, Lena and Diego from NeoQuest.
[00:10] Priya: yeah hi thanks Maya, uh short intros — I'm Priya, I run the search product, Omar does the model infra and Lena is CTO, Diego is our SRE.
[00:17] Maya: great thanks. The objective for today's call is to understand your hosting constraints, throughput targets and success criteria for embeddings + rerank pilot. Daniel from our SE team will go into the architecture questions.
[00:28] Daniel: hi everyone, quick note — I'll ask about your current vector DB, indexing patterns, and tail latency SLOs, then sketch hosting options (hosted / dedicated / private) and tradeoffs.
[00:40] Omar: current infra is self-hosted Milvus cluster, about 8 shards, 3 replicas, documents are product pages — about 500k records. We embed with an internal encoder producing 768 dims today. Retrieval is hybrid: top-100 from milvus + elastic, then a small reranker model that hits the text.
[01:02] Priya: key thing for us is rerank tail latency — we want 95th < 250ms, ideally 150ms. Cost is second but important; we also need to keep data in our VPC for some regulated customers.
[01:18] Daniel: okay good — so two axes: latency and hosting model. For Hosted you get fastest time to start and incremental cost, but network hop to your milvus could add 20-100ms depending on region. Dedicated gives predictable GPU pools we can colocate in the same cloud region as your DB, and Private gives you full VPC overlay with control.
[01:40] Lena: when you say colocate, do you mean Redwood Dedicated can be set up in the same VPC or same AZ? Our security team prefers VPC peering or Private option.
[01:50] Samir: quick clar — Dedicated supports VPC peering and can be set up in the same region; Private is for when you need a customer-controlled control plane or on-prem. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools but control plane is still in Redwood's infra.
[02:05] Diego: our main worry is the embedding fanout — we currently do embed+fanout to Milvus for vectors and also store text in Elastic. If we move rerank to Hosted, we'd incur egress round-trips. Any advice on where to run the reranker?
[02:20] Daniel: common pattern: keep vector DB close to your storage for top-k recall, but run rerank where the model lives to avoid moving big chunks of context. If you keep reranker in Redwood Dedicated next to a milvus cluster in same region, you minimize RTT. Alternatively, you can run embeddings/forward pass in your VPC via Private deployment and call Redwood's Hosted rerank endpoint — but that gets complex.
[02:45] Priya: can you quantify the latency hit for a Hosted rerank flow? say we get 100 qps and top_k=100, reranker is 3-5 forward tokens?
[02:55] Daniel: rough numbers — network RTT 30-80ms (varies), model forward maybe 60-120ms depending on size and batch. If you stream or do batching, we can push qps, but single-request tail might be 150-300ms for hosted if vector DB is remote. Dedicated colocated can get that under 150ms typically.
[03:20] Omar: batching is interesting — we have bursty traf, peak ~250 qps for search, sustained 60-100 qps. How does Redwood handle batching vs latency SLOs?
[03:32] Daniel: our runtime does continuous batching and you can configure latency SLOs. For rerank we often suggest a small batch threshold (2-8) to preserve tail latency. For embeddings ingestion, larger batches help throughput. We can share optimal config for your workload.
[03:48] Priya: about embedding dim — we're on 768 now but exploring 1536 for better recall on long product descriptions. How big does cost jump vs latency?
[03:58] Samir: dimensionality affects index size and vector DB search cost linearly-ish; embeddings compute cost also rises. Hosting side: bigger dims increase memory per vector and slightly increase forward time, but rerank model size matters more. Many customers do 768->1536 experiments: 2–3x storage and slightly higher compute. We can help run quality vs cost evals.
[04:20] Lena: and quantization? we've heard about int8 or 4-bit embeddings — do you support that?
[04:26] Daniel: we support quantized model variants for hosting to reduce GPU memory and cost; for embeddings you can quantize index on the vector DB side as well. There's some quality tradeoff; we can recommend quant profiles based on your eval set.
[04:40] Omar: about integration — we use a custom pipeline that calls milvus then hits our reranker. How invasive is integrating Redwood?
[04:48] Maya: integration is usually two API calls: embeddings generation (or you can bring precomputed vectors) and a rerank/generate endpoint. For Dedicated/Private we offer private endpoints or VPC peering so calls stay inside your network. We also support SAML SSO and audit logs that your security team needs.
[05:05] Priya: what about caching? we have lots of repeated prefixes and recency is important. Could we do prefix/KV caching with Redwood?
[05:12] Daniel: yes we have prefix and KV cache options; prefix caching helps for conversational or repeated queries. That reduces model invocations significantly for hot queries. For vector lookups, you might still fetch top-k but rerank can be short-circuited for cache hits.
[05:30] Diego: a security question — do you support KMS/HSM for keys and are audit logs exportable to our SIEM?
[05:36] Samir: yes KMS integration and audit logs are supported on Dedicated and Private; Hosted also supports encryption at rest and transit, and we can share SOC 2 docs. Logs can be exported or streamed to customer SIEM for enterprise plans.
[05:50] Priya: ok good. Next — benchmarking. We want a realistic pilot: 500k docs, simulate our query distribution with 200 qps bursts, and measure 95th latency end-to-end for rerank. What do you need from us?
[06:02] Daniel: the essentials: sample dataset (500k or subset), a 200-query set reflecting hot and tail queries, and prefer test milvus snapshot or access. Also, what vector dim and rerank model you want us to test. We can run two tracks: hosted quick-run and dedicated colocated run.
[06:18] Omar: we can provide dataset and will try 768 and 1536 dims. Reranker is currently a small BERT variant — maybe 4–6M params? (transcription: 'four to six mil')
[06:29] Samir: small correction: BERT-base is heavier, sounds like you're on a smaller distilled model; that should be fine. For rerank latency, we can test with both 1 and 2 stage rerank and with fanout of top-50 and top-100.
[06:45] Priya: what about pricing — rough pilot numbers for hosted vs dedicated?
[06:50] Maya: I'll send a pilot sheet but high-level: Hosted is usage-based (per-token/per-embedding) which is quick to start; Dedicated is committed monthly with predictable unit economics and lower per-op cost at scale; Private has a platform fee. I'll include a worked example for your 500k dataset and expected qps.
[07:05] Diego: can you also include the networking diagram for VPC peering and required firewall rules? Our infra team will need that.
[07:12] Maya: yes will do, we'll attach a network diagram and sample infra checklist.
[07:16] Lena: any gotchas around high fanout? when we do top-500 retrieval then rerank, that's expensive. We prefer hybrid approach — early recall with smaller fanout and then rerank.
[07:26] Daniel: agreed — typical pattern is hybrid retrieval with semantic vector top-k (50–100) followed by a small rerank. Some customers do cascade rerank: cheap filter first, then expensive re-rank only on shortlisted docs. That usually hits cost and latency sweet spot.
[07:40] Omar: question — can Redwood's runtime do local KV cache inside the Dedicated pool so reranker doesn't have to fetch context every time?
[07:48] Daniel: yes, we have local KV/prefix caching options and cache warming strategies. For Dedicated you can pin models and caches to nodes to avoid cross-node fetches.
[07:58] Priya: what about data residency — if we need everything to stay inside our VPC, is Private the only option?
[08:04] Samir: Private is the straightforward way for strict residency (control plane in your network). Dedicated with VPC peering can also meet many compliance needs, but for air-gapped or fully on-prem we recommend Private. We'll include a compliance comparison doc.
[08:18] Diego: any traction with Milvus specifically? do you have connectors or recommended index types?
[08:24] Daniel: we have customers using Milvus; recommended index depends on dim and recall: IVF-PQ for larger dims with PQ/quant, HNSW for smaller dims and low-latency. We'll include recommended index settings for 512/768/1536.
[08:40] Priya: lovely. last things — timeline: we'd like to run pilot in two weeks and decide by end of month. Are those schedules realistic?
[08:49] Maya: yes — quick hosted proof in a few days once you share data; dedicated pilot (provisioning and colocation) can be ready within 7–14 days depending on approvals.
[08:58] Lena: okay thanks — let's recap next steps.
[09:02] Maya: recap: Maya will send pilot pricing, security docs, network diagram by 2027-01-07; Priya will share dataset+queries by 2027-01-08; Daniel will prepare benchmark script and run the smoke within the week and plan a 2-hour benchmark during week of 2027-01-11.
[09:20] Priya: perfect, thanks everyone.
[09:23] Maya: thank you all, we'll follow up in email and schedule the benchmark slot.
[09:27] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions had a few mislabels (model sizes and acronyms), some crosstalk at 06:29 and 07:40. References shared: link to pilot pricing sheet (link: /decks/neoquest-pilot-pricing.pdf), network diagram to be attached, security pack (SOC2, KMS guide).
